title: SF1186 (2023-2024 Regular): Criminal background checks for firearms transfers; grounds for disqualification of a transferee permit modification

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2023-02-01; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/93/2023/0/SF/1186/versions/0/)
provenance.note: As filed (Introduction, 2023-02-01); official copy from revisor.mn.gov. The bill text is identical to MN-SF-1184-2023 and MN-SF-1186-2023 (same body, different author). Strikes the old rule that only a legal bar could be the basis to refuse a permit, the transfer-report exemption for permit holders, the transferee-permit step after a report, and the old identity-check subdivision. Family and immediate-family transfers and several others are excluded in subd. 6 (not all quoted). No passage vote on file.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 4): (a) The chief of police or sheriff shall refuse to grant a transferee permit if the applicant is prohibited by state or federal law from possessing a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon or is determined to be a danger to self or others under paragraph (b).
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 4): (b) A chief of police or sheriff shall refuse to grant a permit to a person who is a danger to self or others. The decision of the chief of police or sheriff must be based on documented past contact with law enforcement.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 11): A person who makes a false statement in order to obtain a transferee permit knowing or having reason to know the statement is false is guilty of a felony.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 5): (a) The chief of police or sheriff shall deny an application if the proposed transferee is prohibited by state or federal law from possessing a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon or is determined to be a danger to self or others under paragraph (b).
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): A person who is not a firearms dealer is prohibited from transferring possession or ownership of a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon to any other person who is not a firearms dealer, unless the transferee presents a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131 and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3): (d) Both the transferor and the transferee must retain a copy of the record of transfer and any attachments to the record of transfer for 20 years from the date of the transfer.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 4): (b) A person who refuses or is unable to produce a record of transfer for a firearm transferred under this section in response to a request for production made by a peace officer pursuant to paragraph (a) is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.
